title: The Folds Must Be Able To Meet

scenes.tts: In a human embryo, the brain and spinal cord begin as a flat sheet of cells on the back. By the end of about the fourth week after fertilization, that sheet has rolled into a closed tube. This is often before a woman knows she is pregnant. So what happens if the tube does not close? The answer starts with distance. How far apart are the edges of the sheet?
scenes.visual: Cross-section: flat sheet rolls into a closed tube, then an open groove with a question mark between the edges.
scenes.narration: In a human embryo, the brain and spinal cord begin as a flat sheet of cells on the back. By the end of about the fourth week after fertilization, that sheet has rolled into a closed tube. This is often before a woman knows she is pregnant. So what happens if the tube does not close? The answer starts with distance. How far apart are the edges of the sheet?

scenes.tts: The sheet is the neural plate. It creases along hinge points, where cells shrink one face and turn wedge-shaped. The edges rise as two neural folds. The folds move toward the middle, meet, and fuse. Then the tube pinches off from the skin, and the skin seals over it.
scenes.visual: Plate creases at a hinge, folds rise and move inward, fuse, tube separates beneath the skin.
scenes.narration: The sheet is the neural plate. It creases along hinge points, where cells shrink one face and turn wedge-shaped. The edges rise as two neural folds. The folds move toward the middle, meet, and fuse. Then the tube pinches off from the skin, and the skin seals over it.

scenes.tts: Why does the width of the plate matter? Think of two people on opposite sides of a wide table, reaching to shake hands. They can lean, but their arms have a fixed reach. The folds are the same. They can rise and move inward only so far. If they start too far apart, they never meet. So before the tube can close, the plate must become narrow.
scenes.visual: Wide plate: folds move a fixed reach and stop short. Narrow plate: the same reach closes the gap.
scenes.narration: Why does the width of the plate matter? Think of two people on opposite sides of a wide table, reaching to shake hands. They can lean, but their arms have a fixed reach. The folds are the same. They can rise and move inward only so far. If they start too far apart, they never meet. So before the tube can close, the plate must become narrow.

scenes.tts: Narrowing comes from convergent extension. Cells in the plate push in between their neighbors on either side. This move is called intercalation. Each step makes a row one cell narrower and longer. Many small steps turn a short, wide plate into a long, thin one. For this to work, the cells must agree on which way is sideways. That sense of direction is planar cell polarity. Proteins including Dishevelled gather on opposite sides of each cell.
scenes.visual: Top view: a block of cells rearranges from five across by two down to two across by five down; polarity bars sit on opposite cell sides.
scenes.narration: Narrowing comes from convergent extension. Cells in the plate push in between their neighbors on either side. This move is called intercalation. Each step makes a row one cell narrower and longer. Many small steps turn a short, wide plate into a long, thin one. For this to work, the cells must agree on which way is sideways. That sense of direction is planar cell polarity. Proteins including Dishevelled gather on opposite sides of each cell.

scenes.tts: Frog embryos tested this idea. The fate of each early frog cell is mapped, so researchers can aim an injection. They put a disrupted Dishevelled into the cells that form the midline of the plate. The plate stayed wide. The folds still rose and moved inward. But the tube stayed open.
scenes.visual: Wide flat plate; a red mark over the midline; the plate stays wide, folds rise and stop short, tube open.
scenes.narration: Frog embryos tested this idea. The fate of each early frog cell is mapped, so researchers can aim an injection. They put a disrupted Dishevelled into the cells that form the midline of the plate. The plate stayed wide. The folds still rose and moved inward. But the tube stayed open.

scenes.tts: Now aim the disruption at the sides instead, where the folds form and fuse. This time, closure was normal. So the signal was needed at the midline, where narrowing sets the distance between the folds. Mice tell the same story. In the loop-tail mouse, the midline failed to extend before folding began, and closure never started. Keep this rule. If the plate stays too wide, the folds cannot meet.
scenes.visual: Reset to a flat plate with the mark on the sides: plate narrows and closes. Mouse: flat wide plate, nothing starts. Final: wide-open beside narrow-closed.
